comparison: Perfect alignment on optical calculations (C158-C161). Both evaluations affirm the optical property calculations as well-supported. Peer review explicitly praises the study for 'calculating the optical properties of the different ommatidia and estimating light sensitivity and spatial resolution limits,' matching OpenEval's assessment that calculations are sound given anatomical measurements.

Perfect alignment on SPC characterization (C185-C189). Both evaluations accept the SPC count and distribution data. OpenEval notes the regional granule shape variation is preliminary but documented, while peer review highlights the novelty of the complete SPC count, noting 'There is no information about the total number of SPCs in the eye of Trichogramma or any other insect.'

Strong alignment on ectopic photoreceptor findings (C5, C96-C112, C230-C235). Both evaluations affirm the presence and detailed characterization of ePRs. OpenEval finds morphological and connectivity data well-supported across three specimens. Peer review explicitly acknowledges the ePR descriptions and notes they are 'decoupled from the eye's dioptrical apparatus.' OpenEval includes C236-C238 (functional speculation) which peer review also addresses.

Strong alignment on novelty claims (C6, C193, C248). Both evaluations affirm the achievement of complete eye reconstruction. OpenEval finds the novelty claim reasonable given the comprehensive dataset. Peer review strongly affirms this, with one reviewer stating the study 'sets new standards' and another confirming 'the first complete cellular-level reconstruction of an insect eye.'

Strong alignment on sensory tissue retention (C3, C242, C247). Both evaluations support the finding about nuclear retention in sensory vs. neural tissue. OpenEval notes this represents a key finding about miniaturization constraints with supporting EM data and comparative references. Peer review implicitly accepts this as part of the miniaturization adaptations, noting the study provides 'remarkable insights towards understanding optimized solutions.'

Strong alignment on cellular composition counts (C1-C14, C20, plus C17-C19, C21-C23). Both evaluations affirm the quantitative anatomical data. OpenEval finds counts internally consistent and well-documented through 3D reconstruction. Peer review explicitly praises the 'very rigorous effort to describe and assess the variation in each cell type' and notes 'The anatomical analysis is fully supported by quantitative numerical data at all scales.'

Substantial alignment on DRA specialization (C4, C119-C125, C243). Both evaluations support the DRA findings with morphometric and connectivity data. OpenEval finds the transitional zone well-supported. Peer review affirms the DRA findings but notes one reviewer suggests 'additional evidence, obtained by other methods' would benefit the claim about the full extent of the DRA, introducing slight uncertainty not present in OpenEval's assessment.

Strong alignment on subcellular organelle data (C86-C94, C174-C176). Both evaluations accept the organelle measurements and correlations. OpenEval finds observations detailed and consistent. Peer review praises the study for providing data 'at all scales, from organelles to cells and ommatidia' and notes the '3D renders are highly informative.'

Strong alignment on photoreceptor organization (C137-C142, C164-C168). Both evaluations support the volumetric data, statistical analysis, and evolutionary conservation arguments. OpenEval notes functional speculation about motion vs. color vision is cited but not tested. Peer review accepts the findings as agreeing 'with the data on lamina circuits' from prior work.

Strong alignment on rim pigment cells (C113-C116, C190-C192). Both evaluations accept the rim cell characterization. OpenEval notes nuclear counting method and acknowledges incomplete reconstruction doesn't undermine basic characterization. Peer review accepts the data as part of the complete cellular inventory without questioning the characterization.

Strong alignment on dioptric apparatus morphometrics (C24-C33, C34-C42, C132-C135). Both evaluations accept the detailed morphometric data. OpenEval finds measurements consistent and notes the optical role of nuclei (C135) is speculative but not challenged. Peer review accepts the data and notes the paper 'goes beyond cell morphology' to calculate optical properties, treating the speculation about nuclei as presented by authors without objection.

Alignment with different confidence levels on UV sensitivity (C171-C173, C170). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct spectral measurements or opsin identification, noting inference is plausible but requires validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the R7/R7' characterization and UV sensor interpretation without challenge, noting findings agree with lamina circuit data.

Alignment with different emphasis on DRA nuclear arrangement (C126-C135). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative optical role of nuclei (C135) despite solid morphometric data. Peer review (R4) supports DRA findings broadly, including nuclear arrangement data, without specifically addressing the optical speculation, treating morphological observations as part of confirmed DRA specialization.

Strong alignment on rhabdom structural details (C76-C85, C143-C149, C153-C157). Both evaluations affirm the structural data and measurements. OpenEval finds morphological descriptions well-documented with polarization detection capability inferred. Peer review explicitly affirms the rhabdom data, noting authors 'confirmed previous known findings about the distribution and internal structure that assists in polarization detection.'

Strong alignment on pigment cell characterization (C43-C54, C55-C65, C177-C184). Both evaluations accept the detailed cellular and volumetric data. OpenEval finds measurements consistent and well-documented. Peer review affirms the quantitative pigment cell data as part of comprehensive anatomical analysis, noting data 'should be a valuable source for future studies.'

Strong alignment on basic retinal organization (C68-C75). Both evaluations support the photoreceptor organization descriptions. OpenEval notes nuclear arrangement clearly shown and lighter R7 rhabdomeres may be fixation artifact. Peer review accepts the organization data as agreeing with lamina circuit data from prior work.

Strong alignment on DRA rhabdom specialization (C143-C149). Both evaluations affirm the volumetric data, microvilli orientation, and correlation with polarization detection. OpenEval notes polarization capability is inferred rather than directly demonstrated. Peer review explicitly affirms the orthogonal microvilli orientation supporting polarization detection as consistent with prior knowledge.

Strong alignment on Trichogramma comparison (C195-C206, plus broader comparative claims). Both evaluations accept the comparative analysis. OpenEval finds the comparison thorough and well-supported with appropriate citations. Peer review notes the paper 'strives to compare the data with previous literature wherever possible,' treating this as a strength without challenging specific comparisons.

Strong alignment on basic morphometric data (C15-C23). Both evaluations affirm the straightforward measurements. OpenEval finds observations well-documented with precise measurements and standard deviations. Peer review accepts these as part of the comprehensive quantitative anatomical data affirmed across all scales.

Strong alignment on comparative rhabdom measurements (C150-C152). Both evaluations accept the morphometric comparisons and functional interpretation. OpenEval notes functional interpretation about polarization sensitivity is reasonably inferred from literature though not directly tested. Peer review accepts the comparative data without challenge as part of the study's strength in comparing with previous literature.

Strong alignment on quantitative cellular relationships (C174-C184). Both evaluations accept the correlations and percentage calculations. OpenEval finds correlations reasonable and functional interpretation appropriately cited. Peer review accepts these as part of the comprehensive quantitative analysis at all scales from organelles to cells.

Strong alignment on microvilli orientation (C83, C146-C149). Both evaluations support the correlation between orthogonal microvilli, polarization detection, and connectivity. OpenEval notes direct polarization measurements not presented, making functional claim inferential though well-supported. Peer review affirms the orthogonal microvilli structure as confirming 'previous known findings about the distribution and internal structure that assists in polarization detection.'

Strong alignment on comparative volumetric analysis (C212-C219). Both evaluations accept the detailed comparisons with appropriate citations. OpenEval notes critical evaluation of potential discrepancies in Fischer et al. 2019 data. Peer review accepts the comparative analysis as part of the study's strength in comparing with previous literature.

Strong alignment on nuclear volume comparisons (C222-C229). Both evaluations accept the volumetric comparisons and genome size explanation. OpenEval notes the mechanistic link between genome size and nuclear volume is correlative but reasonable and cited. Peer review accepts the interpretation without objection as part of the comparative analysis.

Strong alignment on evolutionary conservation (C162-C166). Both evaluations support the synthesis of observations with evolutionary context. OpenEval finds the conservation argument well-supported by detailed morphological data showing maintained cellular distinctions. Peer review accepts the evolutionary interpretation through affirmation of the comprehensive anatomical analysis.

Strong alignment on summary conclusions (C244-C246, C242). Both evaluations strongly affirm the key findings. OpenEval finds the match with connectivity patterns validates morphological observations. Peer review strongly affirms these conclusions, with reviewers stating the study 'sets new standards' and provides 'remarkable insights,' explicitly praising the integration with connectivity data.

Strong alignment on comparative morphology (C117-C118). Both evaluations accept the comparative statements with appropriate citations. OpenEval finds the morphological comparison straightforward and consistent with measurements. Peer review accepts the comparative analysis as part of the study's strength in comparing with previous literature.

Strong alignment on mitochondrial differences (C207-C211). Both evaluations accept the documented differences with appropriate citations. OpenEval notes identification of possible residual bodies is appropriately qualified as inference. Peer review accepts the comparative data without questioning the observations or interpretations.

Alignment with different confidence levels on R7/R8 volume ratio interpretation (C220-C221). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the morphological difference is clear but functional interpretation is speculative without opsin identification or spectral measurements. Peer review accepts the comparative data as SUPPORTED without specifically addressing the mechanistic speculation about opsin expression.

Strong alignment on electron density observations (C190-C192). Both evaluations accept the observations combined with functional inference. OpenEval finds electron density observation clear from figures with appropriately qualified cross-species developmental comparison. Peer review accepts the rim pigment cell data without questioning the electron density observations or developmental context.

Alignment with different confidence levels on ePR functional roles (C236-C238). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting functional roles are speculative and developmental comparison is complicated by lack of larval photoreceptors in Trichogrammatidae, requiring functional validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the ePR characterization without specifically challenging the functional speculation, though the speculation is acknowledged as part of the description.

Strong alignment on cone cell morphometrics (C34-C42). Both evaluations accept the 3D reconstruction data and volumetric measurements. OpenEval finds morphological descriptions detailed and consistent, noting large standard deviation for DRA cone cells may reflect transitional zone ommatidia. Peer review accepts the detailed morphometric data on the dioptric apparatus without questioning the measurements.

Strong alignment on secondary and tertiary pigment cells (C55-C67). Both evaluations accept the cell counts, volumetric data, and morphological observations. OpenEval notes regional granule shape variation is preliminary but documented. Peer review affirms the quantitative pigment cell data as part of the comprehensive anatomical analysis.

Partial alignment on nuclear arrangement in DRA (C132-C135). OpenEval addresses these claims in R6 rating as UNCERTAIN due to speculative optical role of nuclei despite solid morphometric data. Peer review R6 accepts the detailed morphometric data on dioptric apparatus including nuclear arrangement, treating the optical speculation as presented by authors without specific objection.

Peer review addresses C169 (motion vs. color vision functional speculation) as SUPPORTED, accepting it as literature-based context. OpenEval addresses C169 within R7, noting it is cited but not directly tested, as part of broader photoreceptor organization evaluation rated SUPPORTED.
